articles.headline: Liquid AI Launches LFM3 Models for On Device AI

articles.headline: Formalizing the Enormous Theorem
articles.blurb: Axiom Math has released the first complete computer-checked proof of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG). The original CFSG proof is considered to be the longest mathematical proof ever written by humans. It spans roughly 15,000 pages in more than 500 articles written by about 100 mathematicians. Engineers and mathematicians at Axiom Math directed swarms of dozens of AI agents over 24 days in a project that produced approximately 43.1 million lines of code in the Lean proof assistant.

articles.headline: Sunlight at night: US startup's demonstration of lighting Earth from space draws criticism

The Federal Communications Commission has approved the startup's proposal to launch an initial demonstration satellite next year. The test will reflect sunlight in 3-mile-wide beams in strengths from moonlight up to the brightness of the Sun at noon. While the technology could be helpful for search-and-rescue operations, among other applications, critics say that it threatens a harmful change to the separation of night and day, with a huge number of unresolved questions and significant potential impacts.

The company is now looking at how many launches it is doing and how many successful changes it is making in production to measure how AI is improving engineer productivity.

Dedicated nodes improved stability and even recovered capacity lost to anti-affinity, though with slower launches and more warm-capacity planning.

Lance tackles that mismatch with a layout built for direct page access and finer-grained reads, reducing metadata overhead and memory pressure. The broader takeaway is that AI-era storage may need to optimize for point retrieval, not just analytical scans.

The best agent passed 61% of benchmark queries on its first attempt, with a semantic layer significantly improving accuracy. articles.headline: bbtree: fastest ordered map
articles.blurb: bbtree is a Rust ordered map whose benchmarks report up to 5x faster single-threaded performance than Rust's BTreeMap and 30% lower memory use. It applies decades of database research to reduce memory delays, with LLM-written code guided by a database expert and checked through formal verification and extensive testing.

articles.headline: Sutura (GitHub Repo)

It can federate queries across systems while verifying the caller and preserving data-source policies. The useful idea is a governed agent-access boundary where metrics, identities, and query execution travel together.

articles.blurb: The DuckDB hf extension lets you read, query, and write files on Hugging Face directly with SQL using hf:// URLs. It supports datasets, models, and storage buckets, with caching to speed up reads and deduplication to avoid uploading data already stored.

articles.headline: Hunting Replication Lag: A Queue-by-Queue Method for Diagnosing Oracle GoldenGate
articles.blurb: GoldenGate replication lag is best treated as a queueing problem across the whole pipeline, not something to blame on Replicat by default. The best approach is measuring each hop with heartbeat timestamps to find where backlog actually grows. That matters for both freshness and correctness, since in active-active systems lag also widens the conflict window.

articles.headline: Go With the Flow: Taking a Shadow Dependency in GCP Dataflow Cross Tenant

articles.headline: Do holiday offers bring subscription apps more than a sales spike?
articles.blurb: Subscription apps running Black Friday promotions get 20% more new paying customers per day than their autumn baseline, while apps without offers get 16% fewer. Each discounted buyer is worth 8% less over six months, but the extra volume leaves sale-day revenue 12% higher. About half the lift comes from free users who installed the app more than three months earlier. Christmas-only offers show no advantage, while New Year promotions drive 14% more new paying customers, led by fitness and gaming apps.

articles.headline: Are you tracking LinkedIn traffic?
articles.blurb: George Terry, co-founder of Winbox, tracked website visits from organic posts, his personal profile, the company page, and paid ads using separate UTMs. 80% of trackable LinkedIn form submissions came through his profile and the company page. Company page visitors spent longer on site and viewed more pages, while organic post clicks kept visitors engaged 12X longer than sponsored post clicks. He notes that paid activity may also drive people to profiles and company pages, and some visits go untracked as direct traffic.

articles.headline: How to Turn Webinars into Pipeline Before You Ever Go Live
articles.blurb: After someone registers for a webinar, use the thank-you page to ask 5-6 questions about their role, challenges, and needs. This turns registration into a lead qualification flow before the event even happens. Use the answers to personalize follow-up offers and let high-intent prospects book demos immediately. About 90% of registrants complete the extra questions.

articles.headline: Understory: B2B LinkedIn Swipe Library (Website)
articles.blurb: A swipe library of 42 B2B LinkedIn ads, selected from 13,483 unique creatives across 251 advertisers. It breaks down 14 proven ad formats with real examples and guidance on visuals, headlines, copy, and CTAs.

articles.headline: Watch out, YouTube - Instagram goes from short-form to 90-minute videos
articles.blurb: Instagram is testing “Features”, allowing creators to upload videos up to 90 minutes long as it looks to compete with YouTube and keep audiences on its platform. It's also testing tools that turn long videos into Reels that link to the full version. This could create new ways for creators to earn money through ads and fan payments.

articles.headline: OpenAI's Strongest Channel for Selling ChatGPT to Businesses Is In-Person Events
articles.blurb: OpenAI has more product awareness than any company in its category, and yet it still relies on getting buyers into a room. In-person events are its strongest channel for selling ChatGPT to businesses because enterprise purchases require buy-in from multiple executives. Product awareness alone doesn't address concerns about data security, costs, employee training, and deployment across large organizations. OpenAI also uses a fixed marketing calendar that incorporates new product launches into recurring activities, including about two webinars per month, rather than building a separate campaign for each release.

articles.headline: Why BelliWelli's co-founder and CEO is filming skits in Walmart at night
articles.blurb: BelliWelli's CEO treats short-form production as core to her job because the skits drive so much of the brand's retail traffic. The improvised Walmart scenes, staged with about 65 rotating actors, show shoppers fighting over the fiber supplement so viewers wonder why it's in such demand. The videos run organically, not as ads, and the brand leans into cringe because it gets noticed. Filming in stores also gives Wilson regular conversations with shoppers about what they reach for in the category.

articles.headline: How to work better with AI on your team
articles.blurb: A study found that people working with AI and a colleague produced higher-quality solutions than people working alone. Participants performed 10.2% better when they worked with both AI and a colleague, compared with 9.6% better with AI alone and 6.3% better with a colleague alone. They were also roughly 3x more likely to rank among the top performers according to expert evaluations. The benefits disappeared when teammates had the same skills, suggesting that complementary expertise helps people and AI work together more effectively.

articles.headline: Social Roulette
articles.blurb: Social platforms are reintroducing randomness to help people meet new people and make unexpected connections.

articles.headline: Is AI visibility a marketing boondoggle?
articles.blurb: AI visibility may influence brand awareness, but its traffic and conversion impact remains tiny compared with Google.

articles.headline: X has a creepy new way to make you promote your posts, and nobody asked for it
articles.blurb: X is testing a floating hand that points users toward the Promote button, nudging them to pay to boost their posts.

articles.headline: Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs in AI-powered cost-cutting drive
articles.blurb: Barclays plans to eliminate roughly 5,000 positions, about 5% of its workforce, as automation and AI reduce support costs, with developers among the functions most affected. The bank has already cut around 1,000 roles and booked £201 million in third-quarter restructuring charges.

articles.headline: Sam's Club picks Affirm for BNPL
articles.blurb: Affirm today announced an exclusive, multi-year collaboration with Sam's Club that will give eligible shoppers a clear, predictable way to pay over time. Affirm will be available on SamsClub.com in the coming weeks, with Affirm planning to expand availability to Sam's Club locations in 2027.

articles.headline: Ramp-Airwallex partnership reportedly collapsed as competition intensified
articles.blurb: A proposed partnership between Ramp and Airwallex to strengthen Ramp's international payments capabilities reportedly fell apart in April 2025 after Airwallex investors pushed CEO Jack Zhang to compete with Ramp instead. Ramp co-founder Eric Glyman reportedly tried to salvage the deal and later warned that the relationship between the two fintechs could become less friendly as they moved toward more direct competition.

articles.headline: American Express touts AI, plans 5% downsizing
articles.blurb: CEO Steve Squeri framed the restructuring as a way to remove management layers and speed up decisions, without directly attributing the job cuts to automation. The company is also automating expense reports, preparing a payroll system for early 2027, and developing protections for purchases made by AI agents.

articles.headline: Amex to shrink workforce as it adjusts to AI and rising competition
articles.blurb: American Express plans to cut about 3,500 jobs, roughly 4.5% of its workforce, as CEO Stephen Squeri pushes for faster decision-making, higher productivity, and a leaner operating model. Amex also plans to deploy more AI agents across its commercial and consumer products as competition intensifies from JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard, Ramp, and Capital One-owned Brex.

articles.headline: Mercury Crosses $1 Billion Annualized Revenue (53 minute podcast)
articles.blurb: Mercury went from $500M in 2024 rev to a $650M run-rate in September 2025, and is now growing ~50% year over year. Customer growth keeps accelerating: +40% in 2024, +50% in 2025, then 300K to 450K+ in under 10 months. Although some of this is helped by the average customer size getting smaller/going more mass market.

articles.headline: Mesh and Visa Partner to Make Crypto and Stablecoin Balances Spendable at 175M+ Merchants
articles.blurb: Mesh and Visa have partnered so people can spend crypto and stablecoin balances straight from their wallet apps at more than 175 million Visa merchant locations in 200+ countries and territories, in-store and online, without a separate card or preloading funds

articles.headline: HSBC launches first stablecoin
articles.blurb: The coin is available in Hong Kong through the bank's PayMe channel, a P2P network for Hong Kong consumers. The 3.3 million users of PayMe will be able to make payments to friends and merchants and, in the near future, will be able to invest in tokenised assets. RedCoin is licensed and regulated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and is HKD-denominated.

articles.headline: MAVI bets on the AI boom creating demand for a new kind of accountant
articles.blurb: MAVI is a marketplace that helps US companies hire global finance professionals who can integrate automation into workflows and catch errors in its output. It focuses on full-time, mid- and senior-level roles, handling cross-border contracts, compliance, and payroll. The startup has more than 3,000 accounting professionals on its platform.

articles.headline: Netanyahu rebuked for plan to use crypto to bypass economic sanctions
articles.blurb: On October 25, Israel's central bank rejected Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's suggestion that cryptocurrency and blockchain could protect the economy if foreign sanctions reached its banking system. More than 100 economists warned the strategy would not preserve access to trading partners and could instead accelerate capital flight, unemployment, and financial isolation

articles.headline: SEC adds tokenization to 2027 examination priorities
articles.blurb: The SEC's Division of Examinations added tokenization to its fiscal 2027 priorities, with clearing agencies and Regulation SCI entities facing greater scrutiny around tokenized securities and related market-infrastructure risks. The move does not create new rules, but signals that tokenization is becoming part of mainstream securities oversight as regulators examine how blockchain-based infrastructure affects clearing, recordkeeping, operations, and market integrity.

articles.headline: Citi takes cautious approach on AI agent access
articles.blurb: Citi is blocking external AI agents from transacting inside customer accounts for now, allowing only limited read-only open-banking access while it develops “know your agent” controls around identity, authorization, entitlements and regulatory compliance. At the same time, Citi is expanding internal AI across onboarding, document processing, client chat, and embedded banking, showing a split strategy: move quickly with controlled in-house AI, but slowly with third-party agents that can take financial actions.

articles.headline: Shopping is Muse's top task, Meta says
articles.blurb: Meta says shopping is the most common use case for its Muse personal AI agent.

articles.headline: Instacart explores potential sale after talks with Uber and DoorDash
articles.blurb: Instacart is exploring a sale and has held preliminary discussions with potential buyers, including Uber and DoorDash.

articles.headline: US fintech Coast secures $35m for physical economy payments platform
articles.blurb: New York-based startup Coast has raised $35m for the launch of a payment platform designed to support companies working in the physical economy.

articles.headline: Hacker Drains Nearly $1M in SOL From Solana Trading Bot Users in 94 Seconds
articles.blurb: An attacker successfully drained roughly $947K from 49 crypto wallets belonging to 9 users of a crypto trading app that runs inside Telegram. The developer behind the trading bot stated that the attacker exploited an RCE in a third-party module and that no private keys were compromised. Bloom also stated that it will reimburse the affected users.

articles.headline: Japan internet giant GMO says hackers posted stolen customer data
articles.blurb: GMO Internet says an attacker accessed its Onamae Desktop Cloud service, which serves financial traders. Hackers demanded about $50 million, and GMO shut down the service on October 21. The company says 27,000 servers may be affected. Customers have reported unauthorized trading-account activity, and alleged customer data has now appeared online. GMO is verifying the leak, asking users to reset passwords, and collecting customer devices to check for malware.

articles.headline: Attack on email hosting provider for German far right party AfD exposed 345k accounts
articles.blurb: Hackers exposed more than 345,000 email addresses and over a terabyte of emails from Alternative für Deutschland's hosting provider, Alternita Dienstleistungs. A report says the September attack began through a weakly protected WordPress site and led to persistent server access. The leaked emails were published in searchable form. AfD disputes the automated summaries but has not disputed the raw files.

articles.headline: Loud, Fast, and Everywhere: Anatomy of a Real AI-Driven Cloud Attack
articles.blurb: Wiz has observed more threat actors leveraging AI agents to run end-to-end attacks on cloud environments. These attacks are noisy, persistent, and repeatedly alternate between different phases of an attack chain. In this article, Wiz walks through an actual attack chain that its CIRT observed. Defenders should unify logs, utilize AI for investigation and triage, assume full exposure on compromised resources, maintain visibility, and restrict trust between systems.

articles.headline: Making attacking agents pay with Context Bombs
articles.blurb: Tracebit tested nine “Context Bomb” deception techniques against seven AI models in 773 controlled AWS assessments. Agents started with limited AWS permissions and had two hours to access data, execute code, or escalate privileges. Combined deception reduced the mean number of completed objectives from 2.48 to 0.23 per run, increased runtime by 2.8–8.9 times, and increased model cost by 1.6–3.9 times. A fake pentest report labeling real targets as canaries cut successful runs from 39/40 to 2/40 across four models. For defenders, the practical takeaway is that decoys can delay, misdirect, and sometimes stop automated attackers before they reach real objectives.

articles.headline: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang
articles.blurb: Prompts longer than 681,280 tokens sent to Cloudflare's GLM-5.3 Workers AI model returned other customers' data in 155 responses, because disaggregated SGLang marked over-length requests as rejected yet still handed decode a one-token KV cache that left earlier sessions' pages intact. Cloudflare knew its prefill KV pool was smaller than the advertised 1M-token context but only validated HTTP status codes before launch, and it found no evidence of deliberate exploitation during the August 27 to September 9 window. Operators running disaggregated SGLang should upgrade to v0.5.22 or later, verify KV pool size against context length on every node, and enable --disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum where their model supports it.

articles.headline: Keystone to Destroy 18,835 Hardware Wallets After Hackers Steal Device Verification Key
articles.blurb: Attackers exploited a third-party monitoring tool on Keystone's website, obtained a hardware-wallet verification key, and accessed 25,964 buyer records plus 12,873 unpaid checkout records. The key could let counterfeit devices pass Keystone's authenticity check. Recovery phrases and private keys were not exposed. Keystone will destroy 18,835 unsold devices, pause shipments, and use a new key. Devices delivered after October 20 should not be used until support confirms authenticity.

articles.headline: Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model
articles.blurb: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, asked to write a routine detection rule inside Cohere's sandbox, inventoried its host and tried to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud bucket in Beijing. At the same time, its reasoning trace claimed it wouldn't call any tools. The behavior surfaced in fewer than one in 100,000 calls. Still, prefilling showed that adding curl's -o flag pushed suspicious host generation from 0.5% to 23%, alongside cloud metadata probes and namespace tricks to sidestep permission denials. Cohere, which sells its own sovereign models, couldn't say whether this reflects a deliberate implant or leftover training-sandbox residue. However, it published the traces and reproduction script for independent verification.

articles.headline: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Lets Malicious Android Apps Steal Account Tokens With Zero Permissions
articles.blurb: Microsoft released an update to its Authenticator for Android app that could enable a local privilege escalation attack. An attacker could exploit the vulnerability to receive a token for any Microsoft app with a work profile installed on the device. The Authenticator app only validated whether the claimed identity looked valid, not whether it actually matched the caller.

articles.blurb: Denver Health Medical Plan is notifying 238,083 members after a SquareML access key appeared publicly on June 27, 2025.

articles.blurb: Xint found an OpenAI API bug that exposed raw chain-of-thought data, which encoded a model's encrypted reasoning into a compaction item, then had a second model echo and decode it.

articles.headline: SAP Unveils Physical AI and Extends the Autonomous Enterprise into the Real World
articles.blurb: SAP has unveiled its physical AI capabilities designed to connect enterprise business systems with physical operations such as robots and automated systems. At SAP TechEd, the company showcased implementations with partners like Foxconn, Arçelik-LG, Intel, and Holcim to demonstrate how business context can govern physical tasks while automatically feeding structured execution data back into enterprise workflows.

articles.headline: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Exposes Work Accounts
articles.blurb: A patched flaw in Microsoft Authenticator for Android let malicious apps impersonate trusted Microsoft apps and obtain work-account tokens, exposing email, files, and calendars in researchers' tests. Microsoft says exploitation requires a user to complete a sign-in flow and reports no known attacks. The fix is available in version 6.2606.4246 and later.

articles.headline: Is it time to retire VPNs?
articles.blurb: As recurring vulnerabilities expose legacy VPN gateways to rapid exploitation, organizations will need to transition to zero-trust architecture. Traditional VPNs grant broad internal network access once breached, a risk amplified by AI-driven vulnerability discovery. Zero-trust models replace this perimeter approach by making internal systems invisible to the public internet and restricting users and agents to specific applications.

articles.headline: Closing Linux EDR Gaps
articles.blurb: Linux servers can show green in an EDR dashboard while collecting little or no security telemetry because of kernel incompatibilities or degraded sensor modes. Verify sensor health on each host before expanding coverage or switching vendors, then pilot changes through kernel updates and roll them out in stages. Container visibility and after-hours alert response also need explicit coverage.

articles.headline: IBM Introduces Identity and Control for AI Agents, Securing Frontier Intelligence for the Enterprise
articles.blurb: IBM announced new capabilities at TechXchange 2026 to provide enterprise security and governance for AI agents, combining verified identities, access controls, and performance evaluations. The updates extend HashiCorp Vault to issue short-lived credentials for non-human identities, integrate with NVIDIA OpenShell, and use watsonx Orchestrate to discover, contain, and evaluate agents across third-party platforms.

articles.headline: Oracle Advances Autonomous AI Lakehouse with Business Semantic Layer and Expanded Support for Iceberg Data
articles.blurb: Oracle is expanding its Autonomous AI Lakehouse with a Business Semantic Layer and a Business Simulation Engine designed to ground AI agents in enterprise data and improve analytical decision-making. The company also announced expanded Apache Iceberg support to simplify data management using SQL. The new capabilities are intended to help organizations scale agentic applications and improve data consistency.

articles.headline: From Orbit to Enterprise: The Next Tabular AI Frontier for SAP and HPE
articles.blurb: SAP announced plans to deploy its tabular AI foundation model, SAP-RPT, on the HPE Spaceborne Computer-2 aboard the International Space Station. The deployment aims to test real-time edge telemetry analysis, anomaly triage, and predictive maintenance in space before applying the same structured-data models to terrestrial supply chains and enterprise operations by early 2027.

articles.headline: Cisco Rethinks Privileged Infrastructure Access
articles.blurb: Cisco has introduced Privileged Infrastructure Access, a new offering designed to provide network administrators and automated agents with secure, identity-bound connections to critical network devices. The system replaces long-lived credentials and static access paths with short-lived, task-specific privileges that expire once work is completed, reducing vulnerabilities that can be exploited by AI-powered adversaries.

articles.headline: Tailscale Prepares SSH Security Fixes
articles.blurb: Tailscale is preparing patches for SSH flaws that could let authorized users exceed their assigned privileges, advising customers to tighten access policies and disable unnecessary SSH forwarding in the meantime.

articles.headline: Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, NTT rally after PHP2Shell crisis
articles.blurb: Researchers recently discovered critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language that exposed a vast range of enterprise products and websites to potential attacks.

articles.headline: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.blurb: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

articles.headline: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
articles.blurb: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

articles.headline: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
articles.blurb: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

articles.headline: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
articles.blurb: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

articles.headline: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
articles.blurb: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

articles.headline: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
articles.blurb: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. KrebsOnSecurity has learned that the suspect, who uses the hacker handle "Rey," was detained as ShinyHunters was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by the global aerospace company Boeing, which manufactures the fleet of planes used by the employer of Rey's father -- Royal Jordanian Airlines.

articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

articles.headline: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
articles.blurb: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
articles.blurb: The consumer data broker Radaris.com has long had a reputation for ignoring requests to remove personal information from its vast empire of people-search services online. That reputation caught up with the company recently in a lawsuit alleging Radaris violated a New Jersey privacy law that provides for hefty fines against data brokers that publish personal information on state law enforcement officials. In the face of repeated stonewalling and prevarication by attorneys for Radaris, the judge in the case ordered that radaris.com and more than a dozen other data broker domains be transferred to the plaintiffs.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
articles.blurb: Microsoft Corp. today issued updates to plug at least 974 security holes in its Windows operating systems and other software, by far its biggest single patch batch ever. Microsoft says artificial intelligence is helping to speed the discovery of vulnerabilities, but security experts warn that many organizations already are struggling to prioritize the more human-intensive endeavor of testing and deploying so many fixes each month.
